_meta.title: Example records — Ontology v0.1 applied to Algebra I, Linear Functions
_meta.status: draft · keys verified programmatically (see 04 §6) · no teacher review yet · all costs modeled
_meta.conventions: Selected-response items always include 'Not sure' (never scored as a belief). Keyed positions across the set: EC-05 = A, EC-04 = B (form A), EC-08 = A/C, EC-07 = Q,R. Parallel forms A/B/C are for simultaneous administration across rows or periods; every key below was recomputed by script before this file was written.

records.subject: mathematics

standard.short_text: Construct linear functions given two input-output pairs
Calculate and interpret the average rate of change

learning_claim.statement: Writes the equation of a line in slope-intercept form from two given points (integer coordinates, no context), unaided.
misconception_targets: substituting the point into the wrong variable

existing_activities.name: Problem set: 'write the equation through the two points' (10–15 items, take-home)
existing_activities.delegability_reason: Closed-form procedure on given numbers; a photo of the page returns worked solutions in the format the rubric expects.
existing_activities.what_it_supports: That the student engaged with the procedure enough to produce a page; whether the work is theirs cannot be inferred from the page.

existing_activities.name: Unit test (proctored)
existing_activities.what_it_supports: Executes the procedure under test conditions — but late in the unit and mixed with everything else.

records.evidence_gap: We cannot tell from the problem set whether the student can execute the two-point procedure unaided, or whether the page was produced by a tool.

verification_items.stem: Write the equation of the line that passes through (2, 11) and (6, 23). Show the slope calculation.
verification_items.scoring_rule: Counts: correct slope AND correct intercept, any correct method. Does not yet: either wrong. Flag: correct equation with no visible slope calculation (ask).

variant_rule.vary: Choose integer m (|m| 2–5, sign either) and b (1–9); choose two x-values 3–5 apart; compute y = mx + b for each.
variant_rule.fix: Integer coordinates; slope not ±1; intercept not 0; both points off the axes.
variant_rule.key_change: y = mx + b for the chosen m, b.
variant_rule.avoid: Points that make the slope 1 or −1 (hides run/rise errors); a point on the y-axis (removes the intercept step).

verification_items.evidence_supported: The student can execute the two-point-to-equation procedure on integer inputs without assistance, on this occasion.
verification_items.evidence_not_supported: Interpretation of slope or intercept; the procedure on fractional or contextual inputs; that the skill is retained beyond today. One correct response is consistent with a student who can do this only with the steps freshly in mind.
verification_items.accessibility_notes: Numbers chosen to keep arithmetic light. Allow graph paper for students who prefer to plot first.

verification_items.stem: The line y = 4x + b passes through the point (3, 20). Find b.
verification_items.scoring_rule: Counts: b = 8. Does not yet: anything else. Flag: b = 20 (treated intercept as the y-coordinate) — a named misconception worth a conversation.

variant_rule.vary: m (2–6, either sign), the point (x from −4 to 5, x ≠ 0), and b (1–12); state y = mx + b for the point.
variant_rule.fix: One unknown parameter only; the point not on the y-axis.

verification_items.evidence_supported: The student treats the equation as a relation that must hold at a given point and can solve for the missing parameter.
verification_items.evidence_not_supported: Computing slope; interpreting b; the forward procedure in EC-01.
verification_items.accessibility_notes: Single number response; no writing load.

review.notes: Needs one Algebra I teacher to run forms A–C and report real minutes.

records.subject: mathematics

standard.short_text: Interpret the parameters in a linear function in terms of a context
Interpret the slope and intercept of a linear model in the context of the data

learning_claim.statement: Interprets the slope as a rate with units and the intercept as a starting value in a given context, and distinguishes which parameter each feature of the situation controls.
misconception_targets: the constant term is 'the first month's cost' / 'what you lose per hour'
any number in the equation is 'the rate'

existing_activities.name: Modelling worksheet: 'write the equation and explain what each number means' (archetype contexts: taxi, gym, phone plan)
existing_activities.delegability_reason: The contexts are textbook archetypes; the 'explain what each number means' sentences are the most reproducible text in the course.
existing_activities.what_it_supports: That the student has seen the phrasing; not whether the number is attached to the quantity in their own thinking.

records.evidence_gap: We cannot tell from the worksheet whether the student attaches the number to the quantity or reproduces the standard phrasing.

verification_items.stem:
A candle's height h (cm) after burning for t hours is h = 20 − 1.5t.
A student wrote: "The candle loses 20 cm every hour, and 1.5 is how tall it was at the start."
(a) Cross out what is wrong and write the correct statement.
(b) After how many hours is the candle 11 cm tall?
verification_items.key: (a) Loses 1.5 cm per hour; 20 cm is the starting height. (b) 20 − 1.5t = 11 → t = 6 hours.
verification_items.scoring_rule: Counts for LC-2: (a) both roles corrected with units or a clear quantity. (b) is scored separately for LC-7 (6 hours). Does not yet: swaps only one of the two; or says 'the slope is 1.5' without a quantity. Flag: (a) correct but (b) blank — interpretation without use.
verification_items.misconception_target: constant term read as the rate

variant_rule.vary: Context (candle, battery, tank, fuel), starting value (12–100), rate (decimal or integer), target value in (b).
variant_rule.fix: Decreasing situation; the flawed sentence swaps the two roles exactly; (b) yields a whole number of units.
variant_rule.avoid: Rates of 1 (a swap becomes invisible); contexts requiring cultural knowledge.

parallel_forms.stem_delta: battery B = 100 − 8t (% after t hours of video); when 36%?
tank L = 96 − 6t (cm after t min); when 30 cm?

verification_items.evidence_supported: The student can tell rate from starting value in a decreasing linear context and correct a swapped interpretation; (b) supports that they can solve for the input.
verification_items.evidence_not_supported: Interpretation in increasing contexts or with a negative intercept; building the equation from the situation (that is EC-10); that the student would avoid the swap in their own writing.
verification_items.accessibility_notes: Cross-out-and-correct keeps writing to one phrase. Provide the frame 'The ___ is the ___ (units)' for multilingual learners.

verification_items.stem:
In homework, a taxi charged a $3 pickup fee plus $2 per mile, so the fare was F = 2m + 3.
Today the pickup fee has doubled and the per-mile rate has not changed.
Which part of the equation changes?   ○ slope   ○ y-intercept   ○ both   ○ neither   ○ not sure
Write the new equation.
distractor_rationale: slope — attaches the fee to the multiplier
neither — reads 'per-mile rate unchanged' as nothing changed
verification_items.scoring_rule: Counts: correct selection AND correct new equation. Does not yet: selection right, equation wrong (or vice versa) — the equation decides. Flag: 'not sure'.

variant_rule.vary: Which parameter changes (fee only / rate only / both), the base fare, the multiplier of the change.
variant_rule.fix: A base equation the students actually met in practice; exactly one sentence of change.
variant_rule.key_change: Selection follows the change; equation updates the changed parameter(s).
variant_rule.avoid: Changes stated as percentages (adds an arithmetic step that is not the claim).

parallel_forms.stem_delta: fee doubled AND rate up by $1/mile

verification_items.evidence_supported: The student maps a feature of the situation (a one-time fee, a per-unit rate) to the parameter that carries it.
verification_items.evidence_not_supported: Interpretation in unfamiliar contexts; computing fares; the selection alone (20% guess rate) — only the equation counts.
verification_items.accessibility_notes: Base problem is familiar, so language load is minimal; this primitive is well suited to newcomers.

review.notes: EC-04 presumes the taxi problem was actually in practice — the teacher must swap in their own base problem.

records.subject: mathematics

standard.short_text: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way
The graph of an equation is the set of all its solutions

learning_claim.statement: Moves between a table, an equation and a graph of the same linear function, identifying slope and intercept in each form.
misconception_targets: slope read as the change in y between consecutive rows regardless of the x-step

existing_activities.name: Desmos activity: graph the equation, screenshot, describe
existing_activities.delegability_reason: Graphing tool does the translation; the description is generic text.
existing_activities.what_it_supports: That the student can operate the tool.

existing_activities.name: Card-matching in class (tables ↔ graphs ↔ equations), pairs
existing_activities.what_it_supports: Group-level fluency; individual evidence is weak because pairs share answers.

records.evidence_gap: We cannot tell from the Desmos task or the pair activity whether an individual student reads slope and intercept correctly from a table when the x-step is not 1.

verification_items.stem:
The table shows a linear function.
x:  0   2   4   6
y:  5   9  13  17
Which equation matches the table?   (A) y = 2x + 5   (B) y = 4x + 5   (C) y = 5x + 2   (D) y = 2x + 9   (E) Not sure
What in the table told you the slope?
verification_items.key: (A) y = 2x + 5. Reason must name 'y goes up 4 when x goes up 2' (or 4/2 = 2).
distractor_rationale: (B) uses the change in y per row (4) as the slope, ignoring the x-step of 2
(D) uses the second row's y as the intercept
verification_items.scoring_rule: Counts: (A) AND the reason mentions the x-step (2) or a ratio. Does not yet: (A) with reason 'it goes up by 4' (correct answer, wrong model — treat as (B)). Flag: Not sure.

variant_rule.vary: m, b, and the x-step (2, 3 or 5); recompute the four options with the same four error roles.
variant_rule.fix: x-step ≠ 1; x starts at 0 so the intercept is visible; distractors keep their roles (row-difference, swap, second-row intercept).
variant_rule.key_change: Keyed option = y = mx + b; rotate the keyed letter across forms.
variant_rule.avoid: x-step 1 (makes (A) and (B) identical); m = b (makes (C) identical to the key).

verification_items.evidence_supported: The student reads slope from a table as change in y per unit change in x (not per row) and reads the intercept at x = 0.
verification_items.evidence_not_supported: Reading the same features from a graph; building a table from an equation (that is EC-06); the selection alone (25% guess rate) — the reason decides.
verification_items.accessibility_notes: Selection format; reason can be a fraction rather than a sentence.

verification_items.stem: For y = −3x + 12: fill in the table for x = 0, 2, 4. Then write where the line crosses the y-axis and where it crosses the x-axis.
verification_items.key: (0, 12), (2, 6), (4, 0); crosses the y-axis at (0, 12) and the x-axis at (4, 0).
verification_items.scoring_rule: Counts: all three y-values AND both crossing points. Does not yet: any wrong. Flag: table right, x-crossing given as 12 (reads the intercept as both crossings).

variant_rule.vary: m (negative, −2 to −5), b a multiple of |m| so the x-intercept is an integer; x-values 0, 2, 4 or 0, 3, 6.
variant_rule.fix: Negative slope (so the x-crossing falls inside the table); positive intercept.
variant_rule.avoid: Slopes where the x-intercept is not a table value (students should be able to *see* it).

verification_items.evidence_supported: The student can produce a table from an equation and identify both intercepts from it.
verification_items.evidence_not_supported: Reading from a drawn graph; interpretation; positive-slope cases where the x-intercept is negative.
verification_items.accessibility_notes: Provide the empty table on the page; no sketch required.

records.subject: mathematics

standard.short_text: Recognize situations in which one quantity changes at a constant rate per unit interval relative to another

learning_claim.statement: Decides whether a relationship shown in a table is linear by testing for a constant rate of change per unit of x, including when the x-values are unevenly spaced.
misconception_targets: linear ⇔ equal differences in y (ignoring the x-step)

existing_activities.name: Homework: 'linear or not?' sorting set (evenly spaced tables)
existing_activities.delegability_reason: Every table has x-step 1, so the surface rule 'same y-difference' gives full marks; a tool or the surface rule both pass.
existing_activities.what_it_supports: That the student can apply the same-difference rule; it cannot separate that rule from the rate definition.

records.evidence_gap: We cannot tell from the homework whether the student uses constant rate per unit x or the surface rule 'same difference in y'.

verification_items.stem:
Which of these tables show a linear function? Tick each one that does, and write its rate of change. Tick 'not sure' if you are not sure.
P:  x 1,2,3,4 / y 3,6,12,24
Q:  x 1,2,3,4 / y 10,7,4,1
R:  x 0,1,3,4 / y 2,5,11,14
verification_items.key: Q (rate −3) and R (rate 3). P is not linear (doubling).
distractor_rationale: R not ticked — the y-differences are 3, 6, 3 so the surface rule rejects it; this is the misconception the item exists for
verification_items.scoring_rule: Counts: Q and R ticked with rates −3 and 3, P not ticked. Does not yet: R missing (surface rule) or P ticked. Flag: R ticked but with rate 6 or '3, 6, 3'.
verification_items.misconception_target: equal y-differences taken as the definition of linear

variant_rule.vary: The three tables' numbers; which letter is the exponential; which letter has the uneven x-step; the sign of the linear rates.
variant_rule.fix: Exactly one exponential-looking table, one evenly spaced linear table, one unevenly spaced linear table with a visible x-gap of 2.
variant_rule.key_change: Rates of the two linear tables.
variant_rule.avoid: Uneven table whose y-differences happen to be equal anyway; tables with only three rows.

parallel_forms.stem_delta: P doubling; Q −3; R uneven, rate 3

verification_items.evidence_supported: The student holds 'constant rate per unit x' as the test for linearity and applies it when the x-step varies.
verification_items.evidence_not_supported: Distinguishing linear from exponential growth in words or context; recognising linearity from a graph or a situation; selection alone (guessing gives R-ticked one time in two).
verification_items.accessibility_notes: No language beyond 'linear' and 'rate'. Works with mini-whiteboards for instant whole-class read.

verification_items.stem:
Two phone plans. Plan A: cost C = 15x + 40. Plan B: cost C = 20x + 10 (x = months).
Without solving or graphing:
(a) Will the two plans ever cost the same?   ○ yes   ○ no   ○ not sure
(b) For a very large number of months, which plan is cheaper?   ○ A   ○ B   ○ not sure
One sentence: what in the equations tells you?
verification_items.key: (a) yes; (b) A. Reason names both: B starts lower (10 < 40) and grows faster (20 > 15), so B must overtake A. (They meet at x = 6 — not required.)
distractor_rationale: (a) no — sees different slopes as 'different lines that never meet' or confuses with parallel
(b) B — picks the plan with the lower starting cost
verification_items.scoring_rule: Counts: (a) yes, (b) A, AND the sentence mentions the slopes (or 'grows faster'). Does not yet: correct choices with a sentence that only mentions the starting values. Flag: any 'not sure'.

variant_rule.vary: Both slopes and intercepts, keeping the plan with the lower intercept the one with the steeper slope; the context (plans, rentals, savings accounts).
variant_rule.fix: Lines that cross at positive x; slopes visibly different.
variant_rule.key_change: Crossing always 'yes'; long-run cheaper = the smaller slope.
variant_rule.avoid: Crossing at x < 3 (students compute it in their head and stop reasoning); equal slopes.

verification_items.evidence_supported: The student reasons from the relative sizes of slope and intercept to the existence of a crossing and the long-run comparison, without computing.
verification_items.evidence_not_supported: Solving the system; interpreting the crossing point; the selections alone (guess rate 25% for both correct) — the sentence decides.
verification_items.accessibility_notes: Offer the frame: 'B starts ___ but grows ___, so ___.'

records.subject: mathematics

standard.short_text: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others
Calculate the average rate of change

learning_claim.statement: Locates and corrects an error in an unfamiliar slope calculation (inverted ratio, inconsistent subtraction order).

existing_activities.name: 'Find the error' homework sheet
existing_activities.delegability_reason: Error-finding on a photographed page is a one-turn task for a tool.
existing_activities.what_it_supports: Exposure to common errors; not the student's own detection ability.

records.evidence_gap: We cannot tell from the sheet whether the student detects the error themselves.

verification_items.stem:
A student found the slope of the line through (1, 8) and (4, 2) like this:
   m = (4 − 1) / (2 − 8)
   m = 3 / (−6)
   m = −1/2
Circle the first line where the work goes wrong. Then write the correct slope.
verification_items.key: First line is wrong (x-differences over y-differences — inverted). Correct slope m = (2 − 8)/(4 − 1) = −6/3 = −2.
verification_items.scoring_rule: Counts: first line circled AND m = −2. Does not yet: circles a later line (arithmetic is correct from line 1 on) or gives +2 or −1/2. Flag: −2 with no line circled.

variant_rule.vary: The two points and the error type: inverted ratio (form A), or inconsistent order (form C), or a sign slip in the numerator.
variant_rule.fix: Exactly one error, in the first line; the arithmetic after it is correct for the wrong setup; the true slope is an integer.
variant_rule.key_change: Correct slope = Δy/Δx with consistent order.
variant_rule.avoid: True slope ±1 (an inverted ratio then looks right); points sharing an x- or y-coordinate.

verification_items.evidence_supported: The student recognises a violated slope definition in someone else's work and can state the correct value.
verification_items.evidence_not_supported: That the student avoids the error in their own work (EC-01 is the check for that); errors of other kinds; performance when several errors are present.
verification_items.accessibility_notes: Three-line stimulus; circling reduces writing. Good for students who struggle with blank-page starts.

records.subject: mathematics

standard.short_text: Create equations in two variables to represent relationships between quantities
Determine an explicit expression from a context

learning_claim.statement: Builds a linear model from a situation in which the rate and starting value are not stated directly, and uses it to answer a question.
misconception_targets: using the first reading as the intercept without checking the time origin
dividing the wrong way round when finding the rate

existing_activities.name: Take-home modelling task (choose a scenario, write the function, interpret)
existing_activities.delegability_reason: Scenario text alone returns a complete model with interpretation (see Track-2 worked example for the quadratic version of the same finding).
existing_activities.what_it_supports: Engagement with the modelling cycle; not unaided model-building.

records.evidence_gap: We cannot tell from the take-home task whether the student can extract a rate and starting value from raw observations and assemble the model unaided.

verification_items.stem:
A hiker walks at a steady pace. At 9:00 she is 3.4 km from the trailhead. At 9:40 she is 5.8 km from the trailhead.
(a) Write a function d(t) for her distance from the trailhead, where t is minutes after 9:00.
(b) How far from the trailhead will she be at 10:00?
verification_items.scoring_rule: Counts: correct rate with a sensible unit AND correct starting value AND 7.0 km. Does not yet: rate inverted (40/2.4), or intercept 0, or t in hours with the rate in per-minute. Flag: (b) correct by proportional reasoning without (a) — reasoning present, model absent.

variant_rule.vary: Context (draining pool, printer paper, fuel, savings), direction (increasing or decreasing), the two readings and the time gap; ask for a time not in the readings.
variant_rule.fix: Rate and start are never stated; two readings at non-zero times, or one at the origin; clean decimal rate; the (b) time is a round number.
variant_rule.key_change: rate = Δquantity/Δtime; start = reading − rate × time; (b) = start + rate × t.
variant_rule.avoid: A first reading at the origin AND a stated rate (then it is EC-01 with nouns); time gaps that produce repeating decimals.

parallel_forms.stem_delta: pool draining: 2,400 L at 2:00, 1,800 L at 2:15; at 2:45?
printer: 500 sheets at 8:00, 380 sheets at 8:24; at 9:00?

verification_items.evidence_supported: The student can recover a rate from two observations, assemble a linear model in an unfamiliar physical context, and use it — a moderate transfer (context and information form changed; domain and modality did not).
verification_items.evidence_not_supported: Far transfer (e.g., a non-time independent variable, or data that must be judged approximately linear); interpretation of the model's limits; fluency on standard two-point problems (a slow but correct method still counts here).
verification_items.accessibility_notes: Highest reading load in the set; one context sentence, glossed. Allow a sketch. Calculator permitted so the claim is the model, not the arithmetic.

verification_items.stem: Write the equation of a line that has a negative slope and passes through (0, 4). Then give one point on your line that is in Quadrant IV (x > 0 and y < 0).
verification_items.key: Any y = mx + 4 with m < 0, plus a point (x, mx + 4) with x > 0 and mx + 4 < 0, i.e. x > −4/m. Example: y = −2x + 4 and (3, −2).
verification_items.scoring_rule: Counts: m < 0 AND b = 4 AND the point satisfies the equation AND lies in Quadrant IV (three quick checks). Does not yet: any check fails. Flag: correct equation with a point in Quadrant I (met two constraints, missed the geometric one).

variant_rule.vary: Sign of slope (then the quadrant changes accordingly), the intercept, the named quadrant.
variant_rule.fix: Exactly three constraints; the constraints together force real use of slope sign and intercept.
variant_rule.avoid: Constraints satisfiable by y = 0 or by a horizontal line; more than three constraints (scoring cost).

parallel_forms.stem_delta: negative slope, through (0, 4), point in Quadrant IV
parallel_forms.key: m<0, b=4, point with x>0,y<0 on the line

parallel_forms.stem_delta: positive slope, through (0, −6), point in Quadrant I
parallel_forms.key: m>0, b=−6, point with x>0,y>0 on the line

parallel_forms.stem_delta: negative slope, through (0, −3), point in Quadrant II
parallel_forms.key: m<0, b=−3, point with x<0,y>0 on the line

verification_items.evidence_supported: The student can use the meaning of slope sign and intercept to construct an object meeting constraints — evidence that the concepts are usable, not just recognisable.
verification_items.evidence_not_supported: Performance on the typical forward problem; interpretation in context; precision of computation beyond the one point.
verification_items.accessibility_notes: Offer the scaffold 'y = ___x + ___' on the page for students who freeze on open tasks.

review.notes: EC-10 is the item most likely to need language adjustment for multilingual classes.

records.subject: mathematics

standard.short_text: Solve linear equations in one variable
Create equations in one variable and use them to solve problems

learning_claim.statement: Solves a two-step linear equation arising from a context to find the input that produces a given output.
misconception_targets: dividing the constant by the coefficient

existing_activities.name: Equation-solving drill set (online, auto-scored)
existing_activities.delegability_reason: Auto-scored drills are solved by any tool in one step; the platform records completion, not authorship.

records.evidence_gap: We cannot tell from the drill record whether the student can solve for the input unaided.

verification_items.stem: A bike rental costs C = 18d + 30 dollars for d days. Someone paid $138. For how many days did they rent the bike? Show one line of work.
verification_items.scoring_rule: Counts: d = 6 with a line showing 138 − 30 or 108/18. Does not yet: 7.67 (divided before subtracting), 138/18 alone. Flag: 6 with no work.

variant_rule.vary: Coefficient (12–30), constant (20–60), and the paid amount (constant + coefficient × an integer 4–9).
variant_rule.fix: Two-step; integer answer; the 'divide first' error produces a non-integer so it is visible.
variant_rule.avoid: Paid amounts divisible by the coefficient (hides the divide-first error).

verification_items.evidence_supported: The student can solve a two-step linear equation in one variable set in a familiar context, unaided.
verification_items.evidence_not_supported: Equations with variables on both sides, fractions, or distribution; building the equation from words (given here); interpretation.
verification_items.accessibility_notes: Single-number response; the 'one line of work' requirement is what makes the divide-first error visible.

review.notes: Included as a deliberately plain procedural claim to test whether the ontology adds anything over a standard quiz item — see 04 and 07.

records.subject: mathematics

standard.short_text: Fit a function to data; use fitted functions to solve problems in context

learning_claim.statement: Given real, imperfect data, decides whether a linear model is reasonable over a stated domain, fits one, and states a limitation of the model.
misconception_targets: any data with a trend is 'linear'

existing_activities.name: Data-collection project (measure, plot, fit, write-up)
existing_activities.delegability_reason: The measurements are collected in class and are not in any prompt; everything downstream of the data table (plot, fit, write-up, limitation) is producible from a photo of the table.
existing_activities.what_it_supports: That the student collected data; the judgment 'is linear reasonable here?' cannot be attributed to the student from the write-up.

records.evidence_gap: We cannot tell from the project whether the student made the judgment 'linear is reasonable over this domain' or received it.
records.no_short_check_reason: The claim is a judgment made over a data set and a domain; a 3-minute item can only present pre-digested data, which removes the judgment. Cheap proxies (EC-07's classification, EC-10's transfer) reach neighbouring claims, not this one. Independent evidence for LC-8 has to come from a supervised extended task (one class period, teacher's own data, no take-home phase) or a short structured conversation at the project's data stage. The product must say this rather than ship an item that pretends to reach it.

review.notes: Deliberately unresolved. Recorded in 04 as the claim for which no cheap independent check could be designed.
